Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer. `jusprin-dev` is the development branch, and `main` is the stable and release branch. Version 2.0.0 is the last published release, tagged `jusprin/v2.0.0`. A new skill, `jusprin-release`, was just written to list every step a release needs, including the steps the release workflow does not enforce. It exists only on local branch `claude/release-skill` (one commit on top of `origin/jusprin-dev`), which your worktree is cut from. It has never been run end to end. You are its first cold reader, and nobody will brief you further. Kenneth is the owner and the only person who may start the release workflow or publish.

Task:
Prepare JusPrin release 2.0.1 by following the `jusprin-release` skill (`.claude/skills/jusprin-release/SKILL.md`, in your worktree) step by step, exactly as written. Load it with the Skill tool if it is listed; otherwise read the file.

This run has two goals: getting 2.0.1 ready, and testing the skill. Follow the skill literally. Where it is unclear, wrong, missing a step or a command, or tells you something that turns out false, do what is right, and write down what happened. Do not edit the skill file itself.

Rules for this run:
- Every action the skill reserves for Kenneth (version number if unsure, release-notes wording, server deploy, API spend, pushing, moving `main`, starting the release workflow, downloading draft files, posting on GitHub, publishing) needs his yes in this session. Ask, then wait. Never publish the draft.
- The branch name `claude/release-2.0.1` and the worktree `.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.1` already exist and belong to another session. Do not use or touch them. Pick another name and record this as a skill finding.
- Several other sessions build on this Mac. Follow the build rules in `AGENTS.md`.

Done looks like: either the draft release for 2.0.1 exists and was tested as the skill says, or you stopped at a step waiting for Kenneth. Either way, write an untracked file `release-skill-findings.md` at the root of your worktree, and never commit it. For each skill step, the file says what you did, what happened, and any problem with the skill's text, with a suggested rewording. Report its full path when you finish or stop.

SKILL.md
---
name: jusprin-release
description: Use when asked to make, prepare or start a new JusPrin release (a new version on GitHub), from choosing the commit range to the after-publish steps. Covers the version, release notes, server readiness, translations, the error-handling audit, tests, the guide check, moving main, the release workflow, testing the draft and what follows publishing. Not for JusPrin 1 (jusprin-v1) or OrcaSlicer's own releases.
---

# Making a JusPrin release

The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes and a guide check
(see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
those too, in the order they have to happen.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
covers that one action, not the next one.

- The version number, when he has not named it.
- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
- Deploying the server.
- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.
- Posting anything on GitHub, such as replies to issues.

**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
Never force-push `main`.

## 1. Set up

1. Find the last release: `git tag --list 'jusprin/v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
   The range is that tag to `origin/jusprin-dev` (after `git fetch origin`).
2. Make your own worktree from `origin/jusprin-dev`, under
   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on a branch named `claude/release-<version>`.
   Never name it `jusprin-release/...`: pushing a branch with that name starts
   an unsigned release build.
3. Read every commit in the range: `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <range>`.
   Note what a person would notice, and the GitHub issues each change fixes.

## 2. Version and release notes

1. Set `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`. It must be
   above every released JusPrin version.
2. Write `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. The app
   shows this file under "What's new", and the draft starts with it. Follow the
   shape of the previous release's file. Write for a person who prints, not for
   a developer. Check every on-screen label you quote against the source
   (`git grep`), and leave out anything you have not checked.
3. A change that sends anything new from the person's computer, such as a new
   message to our server, goes in the notes and says what it holds.

## 3. Server readiness

The app calls JusPrin's server at `https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Every address
the release calls must already be deployed there.

```bash
git grep -h -o '"/ent/jusprin/v2/[a-z_/]*' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*' | tr -d '"' | sort -u
```

GET each one: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://jusprinv2.obico.io<path>`.
Any answer but 404 (200, 401, 403, 405) means the address is there. A 404
means it is not deployed. Find the server change in the tsd-enterprise
repository (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`), tell Kenneth what is
missing, and wait until it is deployed. Also tell him about any other server
behavior a change in the range relies on, such as a new error code.

## 4. Translations

1. Run `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`. It
   needs GNU gettext and `npm ci` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`. If it
   changes any catalog, those changes go into the release commit.
2. Translate every new entry in every language, following "Localization &
   translations" in `AGENTS.md` and the `orca-translations` skill.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass: it fails
   while an entry is untranslated or a translation lost a placeholder.
4. Count the entries marked `# Needs human review` in
   `Localization/native/*.po` and `Localization/pages/*.po`. Tell Kenneth the
   count, so he can decide whether someone should read a language.

These steps cannot find a sentence nobody marked for translation. While
reading the range, look for text a person reads that is not marked.

## 5. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, audit the tsd-enterprise range too. Report the findings to
Kenneth. A fix lands on `jusprin-dev` as its own commit, and the steps above
are then repeated for the new range.

## 6. Tests

Build in your worktree, in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`: check the load first, use `-j4`, choose every target before
you start. Configure with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON`.

- macOS: build `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, `shell_integration_harness`,
  `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs`, then run both test programs and
  `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.
- Windows and Linux: the release workflow compiles them but runs no tests.
  Run `agent_bridge_tests` and `jusprin_tests` on each. Kenneth keeps test
  machines for both; ask him for access if you do not have it, and say in
  your report if they were not run.
- When the range changes text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool
  descriptions, tool results, how history is sent), run the live prompt suite
  (`tests/project_prompt/README.md`, and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer
  chats changed). Its `claude-cli` backend costs no API money. Any run that
  spends API money needs Kenneth's yes first.

Report each failure with its output. A failure in the range is a bug to fix
on `jusprin-dev` before the release, not a reason to skip the step.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the build from step 6
with the new version already in `Version.hpp`.

1. Tell Kenneth first: the command drives the app on this computer's screen
   for about a minute a page, so nobody should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` and fix what it reports until it
   passes. It then writes the version to `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`.
3. Look through `git log <range> -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` for new screens or
   menu items no page mentions, and add them to the guide.

## 8. Commit and land

1. Commit the version, the notes, the catalogs and the guide files on your
   branch. Make sure no temporary working docs or screenshots are in it.
2. With Kenneth's yes, land it on `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit: rebase
   onto `origin/jusprin-dev`, then `git push origin HEAD:jusprin-dev`. Then
   bring the main checkout along: `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`.
3. With Kenneth's yes, move `main` to the same commit:
   `git push origin origin/jusprin-dev:main`. This only succeeds as a fast
   forward. If it is refused, stop and tell Kenneth. Never force it.

## 9. Start the release workflow

Only Kenneth's GitHub account may run it; check with `gh api user -q .login`.
With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
```

Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses a Mac app that is not signed and
notarised. Wait for the run in the background (`gh run watch <id>`). A failed
run is a failure to report with its log, not a reason to tick a skip box.

## 10. Test the draft

The draft holds the Windows installer and portable zip, the Mac disk image,
the Linux AppImage and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These files are what people will get,
so test them, not a local build. Ask Kenneth before downloading them.

On each platform: install over the previous release and start the app. Check
that Preferences shows the new version, sign in, have one chat, slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered (for example a
locale bug on Windows, where it always shows). Send one error report if the
release changed reporting.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform and what was not. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Reply to and close the GitHub issues the release fixes, with Kenneth's yes.
- Update JusPrin's Homebrew cask to the new version, if the cask is in
  Homebrew.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise
  repository for new failures from the new version.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

=== 3c134d39e3 Report every failure a person cannot act on; keep a sentence only where they can
An error is expected only when the person can do something about it and
Kenneth decided what they are told. Every other failure now stops the work,
travels up unchanged and is reported once, by the handler at the top of its
entry point, and the person reads "Something went wrong on our side".
Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing
about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as
much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause
analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

Top handlers
- reported(doing, body), in Support/ErrorReport.hpp, wraps every CallAfter
  body, timer, HTTP callback and thread JusPrin's own code starts. Before,
  an exception from a CallAfter or a timer ended the main loop, and one from
  an HTTP callback or a thread called std::terminate: a model list entry
  without "id" aborted the app at launch (exit 134).
- report_unexpected_error moves itself to the main thread when called from
  another. A failure the person already answered in this run is not asked
  about again, so its dialog cannot reopen itself; automatic reports, which
  open no dialog, still send each one.
- An exception leaving any other native event stays OrcaSlicer's, as
  Kenneth decided; GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop is unchanged.

AI requests
- A failed request names its cause only where the person can act. On a
  JusPrin account, by the gateway's error code: signed out, out of credits,
  app too old, request too large, too many requests. With their own key, by
  the HTTP status alone: 401, 413, 429. No answer at all says the service
  could not be reached.
- Every other answer, an error the service sends inside a reply, and a reply
  cut short or unreadable throw UnexpectedServiceAnswer with the service's
  status, request id and body. The sentences for an overloaded, unavailable,
  timed-out, paused or cut-short service are deleted, and
  StreamEvent::Kind::Incomplete with them. The model declining to answer
  (stop reason "refusal") keeps its sentence: it is the model's answer, not
  a failure.
- A tool call that fails in the app's own work still goes to the AI model,
  and is also reported when automatic reports are on, with no dialog. A file
  the person picked that OrcaSlicer will not read answers "refused" and is
  not reported. When the saved projects cannot be read, the call's message
  carries the file system's reason.
- An AI service set up in another window during a reply is installed once
  the reply ends, instead of being dropped.

Account, sign-in and settings
- An account, account box, model list or sign-in answer that is the
  server's fault (a 5xx, or an answer the app cannot read) is reported. No
  answer and a 4xx refusal keep their sentences.
- A key or a sign-in the settings file could not keep throws. The "works
  until restart" warning and its row are gone.
- Delete account waits while a printer or filament chat replies, as it
  already did for the project chat.
- "Sign in" runs the web view's own address check, as "Sign up free" does.
  An address that check passes and the server refuses now reads
  "“alex@gmail” is not a complete email address. Check it, then try again."
  with the address the person typed. The password path is unchanged.

Chats, attachments and saves
- A chat checkpoint, chat switch, restoration or new chat whose save fails
  throws the autosave's own error instead of a sentence made up for it.
  Attachment blobs, attachment folders, the chat-titles file and a stored
  chat state that cannot be read or written throw with the file system's
  error. The timer's own checkpoint leaves alone the one failure the
  autosave has just recorded and already shows as "Couldn't save".
- A message or action a newer build wrote is kept as written and not shown,
  instead of being read as another kind.
- A file dropped on Home is copied with write_file (Support/Files: write,
  then rename), so a write the file system cuts short is an error and not a
  shorter file.

Home and Print history
- A print report answer nobody decided is reported. A refused report shows
  the next step: an ended sign-in shows the chat's sentence for it, an
  unreadable photo "That photo could not be read."
- A photo over 20 MB is refused when it is chosen: "That photo is larger
  than 20 MB. Choose a smaller photo, then send the report again."
- While the projects folder cannot be read, Print history shows Home's
  sentence, "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying.",
  keeps no history, and lists again by itself once the folder can be read.
- An exported G-code file is "not found" only when its path is not there;
  any other failure to read it is reported.
- A printer window whose secure connection cannot be checked says "The
  printer at %s answered, but JusPrin couldn't check its secure connection.
  If the printer's address starts with https://, change it to http:// in
  Printer settings, then try again." Checked on macOS only: on Windows and
  Linux an https address on a printer that only speaks http probably still
  says "Nothing answered".

Start report
- When the server answers the app's start report with a fault, the app
  reports it through report_if_automatic: sent only when automatic reports
  are on, and no dialog opens. When nothing answers (no network, a refused
  connection, a timeout) nothing is reported. Before, both cases only wrote
  a log line. report_if_automatic now moves itself to the main thread, as
  report_unexpected_error does. Kenneth, 2026-11-16, quoting the proposal
  back: "My proposal, not built: no dialog, and a report only when the
  server answers with a fault and the person has automatic reports on.
  Having no network at start stays silent. - go with your proposal".

Kenneth accepted the three new sentences (photo too large, incomplete
address, secure connection) on 2026-11-16: "Yes, all three". They and "That
photo could not be read." are in the catalogs, AI translated in all 22
languages.

Shell harness: new modes --delete-account-waits and --printer-window; the
dialog closer answers only the innermost modal dialog; the stand-in server
answers the account box with 204, as the server does; checks count the app
log's "Unexpected error while" lines where a folder cannot be read or
written; print_history_stopped_print_has_no_row replaces a check that
expected a "Started" row removed on 2026-11-08; the detach check installs an
agent the profile does not pick with --fake-printer too.

=== fbf378bc94 Shell harness: open the printer chat through the shell, as the app does
Several shell harness modes (--printer-setup, --printer-chat-sheet,
--print-host-check, --printer-network-check, --printer-connect-skill)
called PrinterPanel::open directly. That shows the panel but skips the
shell, which in the app hides Home and the project tabs and gives the
chat the whole window. So the harness window showed Home squeezed into
the left half with the chat beside it, a layout no person ever sees.
The real app was checked by opening the printer chat three ways; each
time the chat covered the whole window.

A new helper, open_printer_chat, opens the chat through
ShellController::open_printer_conversation, the path Home and the header
use. The shell opens no chat while one is open, so the helper first
closes an open chat and waits until its close (which finishes on a later
event turn) is done. It then checks that the chat is shown and that Home
is hidden.

Tested on macOS:
- --printer-setup: 348 checks pass, 0 fail. With the old direct opening
  put back, 6 of the new "chat covers Home" checks fail.
- --print-host-check and --printer-chat-sheet: pass.
- --printer-connect-skill: the new checks pass; 3 other checks
  (skill_add_settled, connect_skill_printer_added,
  connect_skill_comes_with_printer_add) fail, the same 3 that fail on
  the unchanged harness.
- --printer-network-check: not run, it needs Bambu's real plug-in.

=== 70f08918d8 Fix two agent tests that failed only on Windows
Two cases in agent_bridge_tests failed on Windows and passed on macOS.
Both mistakes were in the tests; the app code they check was right.

"pick_attachment opens the dialog for one kind and stages the chosen

=== d010a88c1a Read printer sizes the same in every language
When JusPrin runs in a language that writes decimals with a comma
(Portuguese, German, French, Spanish, Russian and others), the add-printer
form showed no nozzle sizes for almost every printer, so the printer could
not be added. GitHub issue TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#39 reports it for
the Flashforge Creator 5 Pro and its 0.4 mm nozzle.

wxWidgets sets the C library's number format to the app's language at
startup. JusPrin's printer catalog read the sizes in the printer profiles
with std::stod, which follows that format, so "0.4" read as 0. With the
number format set to Portuguese, 412 of 454 printer models lost their
nozzle sizes, and fractional bed sizes were cut short (233.5 mm read as
233). The same mistake read a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF as 0, and
told the AI about a nozzle mismatch as "0,2" instead of "0.2".

On macOS the bug is usually hidden: an app opened from Finder has no LANG
setting, and the bundled Python's startup then resets the whole C locale
to "C". Python does this only on Unix, so Windows always shows the bug.

The catalog, the printer backend and the 3MF facts now parse with
OrcaSlicer's locale-independent string_to_double_decimal_point and
atof_decimal_point. The mismatch text is written by the JSON library
instead of snprintf. The test programs compile LocalesUtils.cpp directly,
as they do the JusPrin sources they test.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
